issues.description: The problem statement (UML and text) specifies acceptSupplyDelivery should take four parameters (supplier name, ingredient name, price, quantity): acceptSupplyDelivery(String, String, int, int). However, both the provided template usage (Main.java) and the reference solution implement and call a three-parameter version acceptSupplyDelivery(String name, int price, int quantity) that omits the supplier name. This discrepancy will confuse students about the expected method signature and cause mismatches with example calls and tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the signature consistent across artifacts. Either (A) update the problem statement (UML and text) to specify acceptSupplyDelivery(String ingredientName, int price, int quantity) and remove the supplier-name parameter requirement, or (B) change the template usage and the solution to implement acceptSupplyDelivery(String supplierName, String ingredientName, int price, int quantity) and update any example calls/tests accordingly. Prefer option (A) if the supplier name is unused to avoid adding an extraneous parameter.

issues.description: The problem statement's UML and textual description specify acceptSupplyDelivery with four parameters (supplier name, ingredient name, price, quantity), but the provided usage in the template's Main and the solution implementation define acceptSupplyDelivery with three parameters (ingredient name, price, quantity). This mismatch in the method signature (missing supplier parameter in code vs. problem description) creates confusion about the expected API and how students should implement and call the method.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the API consistent across artifacts. Either update the problem statement to specify acceptSupplyDelivery(String ingredientName, int price, int quantity) (removing the supplier parameter), or update the template and solution to implement acceptSupplyDelivery(String supplierName, String ingredientName, int price, int quantity) and adjust all example calls (e.g., in Main) accordingly. Ensure the UML, textual description, template examples, and solution use the same parameter list and parameter names.
